subject: Renewal incentives grid + SLA offset options
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@omnitech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@omnitech.com; daniel.hsu@omnitech.com
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — incentives + SLA flexibility

Kimberly,

Thanks for the renewal materials you sent last week. We’re generally happy with Redwood’s performance but Procurement has pushed back on the proposed uplift and the effective rate increase for year 2. We need to present a couple of realistic options to our CFO next Thursday.

Two asks from my side to make that deck work: one, can you provide a compact incentives grid (tradeoffs between term length, commit, and one-time credits)? Two, we need clarity on whether some SLA credits can be converted into one-time onboarding or credits for burst capacity during migration windows.

We’re hoping to avoid an RFP but need to be concrete. Can Rafael or someone on your side share scenarios today?

Thanks — Elena
Director, Cloud Platform
OmniTech

[Attachment: OmniTech_Licensing_Details.pdf (pdf)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@omnitech.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com; priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — incentives + SLA flexibility

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. Rafael and I just sketched three scenarios and a short mutual action plan. I’m attaching a single-sheet incentives grid and an SLA-offset term sheet for your procurement team to review. High level: 1) 12m term + modest uplift with a $50k one-time onboarding credit; 2) 24m term + tiered commit (10% lower effective rate) with a $75k credit and capped overage protection; 3) 36m enterprise lock (largest discount) with quarterly true-ups and an SLA-offset option we can convert to a migration burst credit up to $100k.

Key tradeoffs (very briefly):
- Shorter term = flexibility, smaller one-time credit.
- Longer term = deeper discount, requires commit cadence and quarterly reporting.
- SLA-offsets: convertible to credits only at contract signature, one-time election.

Next steps: Rafael will drop the incentives grid in Excel and I’ll set a 30-min call with Procurement at 3pm PT tomorrow if that works. If Procurement wants to see legal-friendly wording we can provide the SLA-offset term sheet as a redline-ready PDF.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: OmniTech_Renewal_Incentive_Grid_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-offset-Termsheet_2027.pdf (pdf)]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@omnitech.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Incentive scenarios — detail + assumptions

Hi Elena —

Posting the details below (also in the attached spreadsheet). I’ve called out assumptions so Procurement can validate quickly.

Scenario A — 12 months (baseline)
- Commit: current commit + 10% uplift
- Effective rate change: +6% yr2 list
- One-time credit: $50,000 applied to next invoice
- Overage protection: standard (no cap)
- SLA-offset: not available

Scenario B — 24 months (mid)
- Commit: current commit + 20% uplift with quarterly reporting
- Effective rate change: +1% yr2 list (after credits)
- One-time credit: $75,000
- Overage protection: capped at 15% over monthly baseline
- SLA-offset: convertible to $60k migration credit, election at signature

Scenario C — 36 months (enterprise)
- Commit: current commit + 35% uplift, quarterly true-up
- Effective rate change: -4% effective vs proposed list
- One-time credit: $100,000 plus 2 free burst weeks (subject to scheduling)
- Overage protection: capped at 10% with pre-bought burst buffer
- SLA-offset: convertible to $100k migration/burst credit, election at signature

Assumptions:
- Volume projections use your Q3-Q4 2026 usage multiplied by conservative growth rates supplied by your team.
- Credits are one-time, non-recurring, and applied within 60 days of contract signature.
- SLA-offset conversions must be requested within the first 90 days of the term and scheduled at least 30 days in advance.

I’ve also included a short example calculation of expected invoice delta for each scenario in the spreadsheet tab "Scenario Examples".

Happy to walk through these on the call tomorrow.

—Rafael
Senior Director, Deals
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: OmniTech_Renewal_Incentive_Grid_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Daniel Hsu <daniel.hsu@omnitech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com; rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@omnitech.com>; procurement@omnitech.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — incentives + SLA flexibility

Kimberly / Rafael,

Thanks for the scenarios — useful and concise. Procurement asked me to validate two points before presenting to the CFO: 1) the mechanism and timing for converting SLA credits to a migration/burst credit (want to ensure it won’t count as recurring discount), and 2) confirmation that the overage caps in B and C are enforced in the billing system (we’ll need a short operational note to pass to our Finance Ops team).

A few quick asks: can you (a) provide a 1-page redlineable term short-form that includes the SLA-offset election language, and (b) an ops note (1-2 bullets) describing how overages are calculated and capped in the portal? If we get those two pieces we can take Scenario B to our CFO as the preferred path.

Thanks — Daniel
Procurement Manager, OmniTech

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Daniel Hsu <daniel.hsu@omnitech.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@omnitech.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — incentives + SLA flexibility

Daniel / Elena —

Short answers and next steps below. Attaching a draft short-form term sheet and an operations note for your finance team.

1) SLA-offset conversion: language below is what we’ll include in the short-form (you’ll see the redline-ready PDF).
"SLA-offset election: At signing, customer may elect to convert up to the agreed SLA-offset value into a one-time credit for migration or burst capacity. Converted credits are one-time, non-recurring, and will be applied to the invoice following completion of the approved migration window. Election must be notified in writing within 45 days of contract signature and scheduled at least 30 days prior to consumption."

2) Overages / cap enforcement (ops note):
- Overages are measured against the reported monthly baseline (defined in Schedule A) on a rolling 30-day basis.
- When a capped plan is in effect, billing will apply usage up to the cap at the normal committed rate; any usage beyond the cap will be billed at the overage rate specified in the order form. Our portal shows a live "cap meter" and we can provide an "api call" for Finance Ops to pull month-to-date usage.

Deliverables: short-form term (attached) and operations note attached. Please let us know if Scenario B needs any numeric tweaks before tomorrow’s CFO meeting — we can run a quick recalculation this morning.

Best,
Priyom Das
Director, Deal Operations
Redwood Inference
